title: Microsoft 365 admin center: agent-level controls for pay-as-you-go
summary: Hold: the table says no agent-blocking API is documented, but Microsoft publishes beta block and unblock endpoints with an Agent 365 licence requirement. The prepaid-credit policy path also omits a named section required by the cited instructions. The roadmap facts and most surrounding billing guidance are supported.

go to Copilot > Cost management . In the banner at the top of the dashboard, select Classic Billing & usage.

go to Copilot > Billing & usage.

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat billing policies create connect pay-as-you-go Microsoft Graph PowerShell API. Read setup-pay-as-you-go, pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot and Cost Management API overview; no classic billing-policy connection endpoint was documented.

claims.quote: When you turn off pay-as-you-go, it can take up to two hours for users to stop being able to use the agents.

claims.claim: The documented billing policy pays for metered usage in its connected service for the covered group, rather than selecting individual agents.
claims.quote: All Copilot Chat or SharePoint agent usage is billed at the per-credit pay-as-you-go rate to the connected Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing itself is disabled by default, so leaving it unconfigured does not start billing.
claims.quote: Pay as you go billing is disabled by default.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope: Users; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go enables SharePoint agent use by people without a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: That resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot license uses a SharePoint agent.

claims.claim: The cited SharePoint page locates agent blocking in the Microsoft 365 admin center Agents section of the Copilot Control System.
claims.quote: in the Microsoft 365 admin center, under the Agents section of the Copilot Control System (formerly known as integrated apps).

claims.claim: No API for blocking or unblocking an agent in Copilot Chat is documented.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api null with the documented Graph beta package block call, POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block, and cite this reference. Document unblock at POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/unblock using https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackage-unblock. State that these preview APIs require a Microsoft Agent 365 licence and delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All permission and are not supported for production applications. The package overview explicitly includes declarative agents: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/overview.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking an agent affects Copilot Chat only, not OneDrive, SharePoint or Teams.
claims.quote: Currently, blocking an agent only affects its availability in Copilot Chat. It doesn't yet apply to OneDrive, SharePoint, or Teams.
claims.fix: Qualify this as blocking agents created in SharePoint, rather than all agents. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-actions#block-or-unblock-agents alongside the SharePoint page: it says blocking SharePoint or Foundry agents only impacts Copilot Chat, whereas blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents also affects other host products, including Teams and Outlook.

claims.claim: Tenant admins and AI admins can manage and block actively used SharePoint agents in this inventory.
claims.quote: Tenant admins and AI admins can manage actively used agents in SharePoint in the Microsoft 365 admin center

claims.claim: SharePoint agent responses respect each user's permissions to the data sources.
claims.quote: For users who access and use an agent in SharePoint, the agent's responses depend on each user's permissions to the agent's data sources.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents sensitivity labels with Purview DLP as a way to prevent selected files from being used by SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: To prevent selected files from being used by agents, use sensitivity labels along with Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP).

claims.claim: Agents can act on a user's behalf.
claims.quote: Agents use AI to automate and execute business or education processes, working alongside or on behalf of a person, team, or organization.

claims.claim: Billing eligibility does not limit agents acting on the user's behalf.
claims.quote: Searched: "SharePoint agents" "actions" "billing" autonomous. Read manage-agents-copilot-chat, manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint and sharepoint-agents-azure-billing; none states this relationship between billing eligibility and action permissions.
claims.fix: Remove 'and billing eligibility does not limit that'. Keep the sourced statement that agents can work on a person's behalf and separately describe the published autonomous-use billing rates.

claims.claim: The billing model is consumption-based Copilot Credits, payable through Azure pay-as-you-go or prepaid capacity, supporting a variable cost rating.

claims.claim: Without pay-as-you-go overage, exhausting prepaid credits makes Copilot Chat unavailable to covered users until the next monthly period.
claims.quote: If you have a standalone Copilot credit policy (not paired with a pay-as-you-go billing policy), when your prepaid credits are exhausted, Copilot Chat is unavailable for users covered by the policy until credits replenish at the start of the next monthly billing period.
